title: Active Learning with Foundation Model Priors: Efficient Learning under Class Imbalance
topic: General Machine Learning->Online Learning, Active Learning and Bandits
claim: A three-phase loop pseudo-labels the pool with a foundation model, filters and samples by imbalance-aware uncertainty, then trains a small model.
layout: 3 shaded phase panels, left-to-right, legend on top, pools above
description: A wide diagram split into three background panels of increasing orange saturation, labeled Phase 1, Phase 2 and Phase 3. A dashed legend at the top defines true, noisy, clean and unlabeled dots. Above the panels sit database icons for the unlabeled pool, the data pool and the training pool, with dotted arrows leading into the phases. Phase 1 shows robot icons for the foundation model and small model. Each predicts a bar chart of class probabilities, and pseudo labels are assigned from the foundation model. Phase 2 has class-count histograms feeding a class weight step, then an uncertainty block. It multiplies the two predictions into a product of experts (PoE), and a diamond Filtering node splits the pool into a noisy set and a clean set. Uncertainty-based sampling then produces the labeled set. Phase 3 shows a neural network being finetuned on the labeled set. The eye goes first to the colorful icons and boxed modules in the center.
caption: The overview of our framework. The framework consists of three main phases: prior labeling, uncertainty-based sampling with imbalance awareness, and small model training, detailed in Section [ref]. Given the unlabeled pool, first phase generates the predicted probabilities from the foundation model and small model, while pseudo labels are derived from the foundation model’s predictions. In the second phase, the clean and noisy sets are constructed based on the imbalance-aware entropy (uncertainty) of the products of experts (PoE). Then labeled set is generated by uncertainty sampling. Lastly, small model is trained to inform the next iteration.
abstract: Real-world datasets across image and text domains are often characterized by skewed class distributions and noisy annotations, which jointly degrade model performance, particularly on minority classes. Among existing solutions, active learning offers an effective and efficient paradigm by selectively querying the most informative and balanced samples for annotation. We propose an innovative active learning framework that mitigates class imbalance and selects the most informative samples to annotate. Leveraging foundation model priors, our algorithm enables imbalance-aware co-decisions between foundation model and small model to tackle noisy and imbalanced labels across various domains. We introduce the first study to systematically explore active learning under the dual challenges of label noise and class imbalance across image and text domains. Extensive experiments on imbalanced datasets demonstrate that our method achieves substantial annotation savings-over 50% compared to the best active learning baseline-while preserving performance and robustness to label noise.
